title: Directional Derivative Of The Value
body_html:
Directional Derivative Of The Value

Let $S$ and $T$ be compact sets and let $f,g:S\times T\to\mathbb R$. Assume that, for every $\alpha\ge 0$, the functions $g$ and $f+\alpha g$ are upper semicontinuous in $s$ and lower semicontinuous in $t$, and that each game $(S,T,f+\alpha g)$ has a value. Then $$ \lim_{\alpha\to0^+} \frac{\operatorname{val}_{S\times T}(f+\alpha g) -\operatorname{val}_{S\times T}(f)}{\alpha} $$ exists and equals $$ \operatorname{val}_{S(f)\times T(f)}(g), $$ the value of the derived game.
proof_html:
Sketch

Let $s_\alpha$ be optimal for player 1 in $f+\alpha g$ and let $t\in T(f)$. Comparing $(f+\alpha g)(s_\alpha,t)$ with the two values gives a lower bound on the difference quotient by $\inf_{T(f)}g(s_\alpha,t)$. Taking limit points of $s_\alpha$ and using semicontinuity places the limit in $S(f)$, giving the lower bound by the value of the derived game. The dual argument with optimal strategies for player 2 gives the reverse inequality.

References

  • [MFoGT, Proposition 3.4.2] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Directional derivative of the value equals the value of the derived game.
